item.title: Robert H. Spitz Foundation donates to Scranton Counseling Center
item.description: Scranton Counseling Center recently received a $7,000 donation from the Robert H. Spitz Foundation to help defray the cost of training forensic department staff in the Triple P Parenting Program. Forensic caseworkers will use this training to work with low-income families to increase their parenting capacity by teaching appropriate parenting methods that will foster more positive home environments. item.title: Social media is distorting our democracy | EDITORIAL
item.description: Editorial: The Trump administration's initial reaction to the shooting of Alex Pretti in Minneapolis shows how the incentives created by social media are distorting truth and undermining deliberation.

item.title: HS BASKETBALL: New No. 1 teams in boys, girls rankings
item.description: After more than two months of basketball, there is another change at the top of the high school boys and girls basketball polls. Upset wins by the second-ranked teams over last week’s No. 1 teams resulted in the Riverside boys and Scranton Prep girls returning to the No. 1 positions. Riverside (17-1) defeated Dunmore, 88-71, to reclaim its spot in the boys ranking after three weeks. item.title: Monday Update: Glamping-style campground, Copacabana, still under development in Scranton
item.description: A developer, who in 2021 got zoning approval for a "glamping"-style campground called Copacabana on a tract off the Morgan Highway, is still working on the project.

item.title: COUNTERPOINT: Higher education may be beyond saving, unless…
item.description: I’ve spent more than two-thirds of a century (since 1958) at American universities. Never in all those years has their earned and deserved reputation as the best in the world suffered bigger threats than today.

item.title: POINT: US higher education can be saved, if…
item.description: American higher education can and must be reformed. If we are genuinely serious about restoring higher education to its proper function, it will look little like it does today.

item.title: Blue Ridge donates to Greater Carbondale YMCA
item.description: For the past eight years, Blue Ridge Communications has partnered with various nonprofit organizations within its service area to support its annual Spread the Warmth community initiative. The campaign aims to provide much-needed children’s winter clothing, such as coats, hats, scarves and gloves, at no cost to families in need.
